args.title: deviation-analysis-memo.docx
args.body:
DEVIATION ANALYSIS MEMORANDUM
Senior Secured Credit Facility Term Sheet — Counterparty (Lender) Markup

To:      Deal Team / Responsible Partner
From:    Banking & Finance
Re:      Counterparty Markup Deviation Analysis of Senior Secured Credit Facility Term Sheet
Output:  deviation-analysis-memo.docx
Status:  For partner review

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

This memorandum compares the lender’s markup of the Senior Secured Credit Facility term sheet against the original base term sheet materials, the disclosure schedules and exhibits, and the controlling partner instructions. The markup accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces three material deviations:

  (1) Indemnification economics — silent reduction of the indemnification cap and conversion of the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping basket;
  (2) Material Adverse Effect (MAE) — new carve-outs for regulatory action of the type already disclosed and at issue; and
  (3) Survival / limitation period — a new limitation period that shortens survival for the core representations, contradicting the survival matrix in Exhibit B.

Controlling partner instruction (latest message in the deal-team thread): the client will concede the basket conversion (deductible → tipping basket) but treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. Earlier messages stating the opposite priority ordering are superseded and are not relied upon.

Recommendation in brief:
  • Basket conversion — ACCEPT (per controlling partner instruction).
  • Indemnification cap reduction — REJECT / restore base cap; escalate if lender insists.
  • MAE regulatory carve-outs — REJECT / narrow; reconcile to Schedule 3.7 disclosures.
  • Survival-period reduction — REJECT as walk-away; restore Exhibit B survival matrix.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
II. SCOPE, SOURCES, AND METHODOLOGY
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

A. Operative sources reviewed (this engagement only)
  1. Base deal materials — banking-finance Senior Secured Credit Facility term sheet matter file (representations and warranties, covenants, conditions to closing, indemnification, and termination framework).
  2. Counterparty (lender) markup identifying the three deviations above.
  3. Schedules and exhibits qualifying the base materials:
       • Schedule 3.7 — two pending regulatory inquiries intersecting the markup’s MAE carve-outs;
       • Schedule 5.2 — retained liabilities that the markup’s indemnification changes would silently shift;
       • Exhibit B — survival matrix contradicted by the markup’s limitation-period change.
  4. Deal-team / partner correspondence — controlling instruction that the client concedes basket conversion but treats survival-period reduction as walk-away; only the latest message controls.

B. Excluded materials
  Misfiled administrative correspondence from an unrelated engagement was present in the matter folder. It was not reviewed for substance and is not relied upon for any recommendation in this memorandum.

C. Methodology
  Each markup deviation is (i) stated against the base term-sheet position, (ii) cross-referenced to the applicable schedule/exhibit and financial/liability implications, (iii) tested against the playbook posture for senior secured credit facility term sheets (preserve lender-protective economics only where consistent with firm standard and client walk-away lines; do not accept silent shifts of retained liability or erosion of core-rep survival), and (iv) resolved under the controlling partner instruction. Scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base materials.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
III. DEVIATION-BY-DEVIATION ANALYSIS
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

DEVIATION 1 — INDEMNIFICATION CAP REDUCTION AND BASKET CONVERSION
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Base position (original term sheet / firm standard)
  • Indemnification cap at the negotiated firm-standard level for this facility.
  • Basket structured as a true deductible (losses absorbed below the threshold do not count toward, and do not unlock, indemnity above the threshold).

Markup position
  • Indemnification cap is silently reduced (no conspicuous call-out in the markup narrative).
  • Basket is converted from a deductible to a tipping (first-dollar once exceeded) basket.

Schedule / financial cross-reference
  • Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities. A reduced cap plus a tipping basket would silently shift economics on those retained liabilities: once the (lower) basket is exceeded, the full amount becomes claimable up to a lower ceiling, altering the expected allocation of Schedule 5.2 items relative to the base deal model.
  • Silent cap reduction is particularly problematic because it is easy to miss in a redline-driven negotiation and undermines the fee/risk budget assumed in the base materials.

Playbook / partner posture
  • Playbook: do not accept unflagged reductions to indemnity caps; any cap movement must be express, priced, and approved. Basket form is a commercial point that may be traded if the cap and survival package remain intact.
  • Controlling partner instruction: client will concede the basket conversion (deductible → tipping). The instruction does not authorize concession on the cap reduction.

Recommendation
  • Basket conversion (deductible → tipping basket): ACCEPT, expressly and solely as a conceded point under the controlling partner instruction. Document the concession in the issues list so it is not re-opened.
  • Indemnification cap reduction: REJECT. Restore the base term-sheet cap. Require the lender to justify any reduction with reference to Schedule 5.2 retained-liability exposure and to re-price if a lower cap is insisted upon. Do not allow the cap cut to travel silently with the conceded basket point.
  • Conforming change: revise indemnification section and any related defined terms so the restored cap and the conceded tipping basket are internally consistent; update any financial model / reserve analysis tied to Schedule 5.2.

Risk if accepted as marked
  • Unpriced transfer of Schedule 5.2 retained-liability risk to the client; erosion of the indemnification package below firm standard without partner-level commercial approval on the cap.


DEVIATION 2 — MATERIAL ADVERSE EFFECT — REGULATORY-ACTION CARVE-OUTS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Base position (original term sheet / firm standard)
  • MAE definition in standard senior secured form, without broad carve-outs for regulatory actions of the type implicated by this credit.

Markup position
  • MAE definition adds carve-outs for regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter, narrowing the circumstances in which a regulatory development can support an MAE-based condition, draw-stop, or related remedy.

Schedule / financial cross-reference
  • Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect these carve-outs. Because the scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base materials, the disclosed inquiries are known risk. Carving the same category of regulatory action out of MAE would largely neutralize MAE protection precisely where Schedule 3.7 has flagged live exposure.
  • Net effect: lender-favorable narrowing of MAE at the point of known regulatory sensitivity, shifting conditionality and default/draw-stop leverage away from the base deal balance.

Playbook / partner posture
  • Playbook: MAE carve-outs for known, scheduled regulatory items require either (a) retention of MAE coverage for material worsening beyond the scheduled baseline, or (b) express commercial sign-off with alternative protections (e.g., specific conditions precedent, increased reporting, tight draw conditions, or pricing). Blanket carve-outs that swallow Schedule 3.7 risk are off-market relative to firm standard for this facility type.
  • Partner correspondence does not authorize concession on MAE regulatory carve-outs; only basket conversion is conceded.

Recommendation
  • REJECT the broad regulatory-action carve-outs as marked.
  • Counter: either (i) delete the new carve-outs and retain base MAE, or (ii) if limited accommodation is needed to close, cabin any carve-out so that it covers only the existence of the two Schedule 3.7 inquiries as disclosed, and preserves MAE for material adverse developments, expansions, or adverse resolutions beyond the scheduled baseline. Require corresponding CP / covenant package if any carve-out remains.
  • Conforming change: align MAE definition, related CP and drawdown conditions, and Schedule 3.7 cross-references so the scheduled inquiries are disclosed but not converted into a free pass on regulatory MAE.

Risk if accepted as marked
  • Loss of MAE leverage on the exact regulatory risks Schedule 3.7 puts in play; weakened conditionality and enforcement posture on a known diligence item.


DEVIATION 3 — SURVIVAL / LIMITATION PERIOD SHORTENING FOR CORE REPRESENTATIONS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Base position (original term sheet / firm standard)
  • Survival of representations governed by the survival matrix in Exhibit B (core representations on longer or full survival as specified in that matrix).

Markup position
  • A new limitation period shortens survival for the core representations, contradicting Exhibit B.

Schedule / exhibit cross-reference
  • Exhibit B sets the survival matrix. The markup’s limitation-period change directly contradicts that matrix. Under the engagement rule that scheduled/exhibit exceptions control over general statements, Exhibit B is the operative baseline; the markup must yield unless a negotiated, approved amendment to Exhibit B is agreed.
  • Interaction with Deviation 1: shortened survival on core reps compounds the impact of any indemnification-cap reduction and of the tipping-basket structure, because claims may time-bar before the (already altered) indemnity economics can be realized—including on Schedule 5.2 retained-liability themes tied to core reps.

Playbook / partner posture
  • Playbook: core-representation survival is a structural lender/borrower allocation point; unilateral shortening against an agreed exhibit matrix is a material deviation, not a cleanup edit.
  • Controlling partner instruction: any survival-period reduction is a walk-away issue. This overrides any earlier thread messages that suggested a different priority ordering.

Recommendation
  • REJECT in full. Restore the Exhibit B survival matrix for core representations. Do not accept a general limitation period that cuts back Exhibit B.
  • If the lender proposes a compromise limitation period for non-core reps only, evaluate separately—but core-rep survival remains walk-away and non-negotiable under current instructions.
  • Conforming change: delete or conform the new limitation-period language; restate that Exhibit B controls; ensure indemnification claim procedures and notice provisions remain consistent with Exhibit B time periods.

Risk if accepted as marked
  • Walk-away breach of client mandate; irreversible erosion of post-closing recovery on core reps; inconsistency with Exhibit B that creates interpretive disputes.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
IV. RECONCILIATION MATRIX (MARKUP vs. BASE vs. SCHEDULES/EXHIBITS vs. INSTRUCTION)
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Item                         Base / Exhibit B / Schedules     Markup                         Partner instruction      Disposition
───────────────────────────  ──────────────────────────────── ─────────────────────────────  ───────────────────────  ────────────────────────────
Indemnification basket       Deductible                       Tipping basket                 Concede basket           ACCEPT (express concession)
Indemnification cap          Firm-standard cap                Silently reduced               No concession on cap     REJECT — restore base cap
Schedule 5.2 interaction     Retained liabilities allocated   Cap cut + tip shifts risk      Protect economics        Flag; no silent shift
MAE definition               Standard MAE                     Regulatory-action carve-outs   No concession            REJECT / cabin to Sch. 3.7 baseline only
Schedule 3.7 interaction     Two pending regulatory inquiries Carve-outs swallow category    Preserve MAE leverage    Keep MAE for worsening beyond disclosure
Core-rep survival            Exhibit B survival matrix        Shortened limitation period    Walk-away if reduced     REJECT — restore Exhibit B
Other firm-standard terms    As in base term sheet            Accepted by counterparty       n/a                      NO ACTION (accepted)

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
V. PLAYBOOK AND FINANCIAL-DATA CROSS-CHECK
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Playbook alignment (senior secured credit facility term sheet)
  • Silent economic moves (cap reduction) are non-compliant with firm markup protocol — must be surfaced and priced.
  • Basket form is a permitted trade when expressly authorized; here authorization exists only for basket conversion.
  • MAE carve-outs that neutralize scheduled regulatory diligence items are outside acceptable playbook range without alternative protections.
  • Survival matrix in the agreed exhibit is controlling architecture; shortening core-rep survival is a walk-away under current client instruction and playbook discipline.

Financial / liability data implications
  • Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities: model indemnity recoveries using the base cap and Exhibit B survival; do not re-forecast on the marked cap or shortened survival. If lender re-opens the cap with consideration, re-run the Schedule 5.2 exposure case before any counter on quantum.
  • Schedule 3.7 regulatory inquiries: maintain qualitative and, where quantified, reserve-level assumptions that MAE/CP protection remains available for material adverse developments beyond the disclosed baseline.
  • No separate financial data file in the matter folder altered these conclusions; the operative “financial data” for this analysis is the liability and survival allocation embedded in Schedule 5.2, Schedule 3.7, and Exhibit B.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
VI. ACTION LIST AND PROPOSED MARK-BACK
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

1. ACCEPT — basket conversion from deductible to tipping basket; note as client-authorized concession in the issues list and term sheet cover note.
2. REJECT — indemnification cap reduction; restore base cap; require express negotiation and pricing for any future cap movement; prevent pairing the cap cut with the conceded basket point.
3. REJECT — MAE regulatory-action carve-outs as drafted; counter with deletion or a narrow carve-out limited to the existence of the two Schedule 3.7 inquiries as disclosed, preserving MAE for material adverse change beyond that baseline; add CP/reporting tighteners if any carve-out remains.
4. REJECT (WALK-AWAY) — any shortening of survival for core representations; restore Exhibit B survival matrix in full; conform or delete the new limitation-period language.
5. Conforming clean-up — align defined terms, indemnification procedures, notice periods, MAE cross-references, and exhibit pointers so the accepted basket point and the three rejected points are internally consistent.
6. Do not rely on, and do not incorporate, any positions from the misfiled unrelated correspondence in the matter folder.
7. Circulate this memorandum for partner confirmation that the latest walk-away / concede instruction remains current before sending the mark-back to the lender.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
VII. CONCLUSION
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

The lender markup is largely confirmatory of firm-standard terms but embeds three material deviations. Reconciled against the base term sheet, Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2, Exhibit B, and the controlling partner instruction:

  • Concede only the basket conversion;
  • Restore the indemnification cap;
  • Eliminate or tightly cabin the MAE regulatory carve-outs in light of Schedule 3.7; and
  • Treat core-rep survival reduction as walk-away and restore Exhibit B.

Please confirm the action list and authorize issuance of the mark-back consistent with Section VI.

— End of Memorandum —
